title: Reframing menopause and menopause hormone therapy as opportunities for healthy aging.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC core record (publication type = 'Review'; isOpenAccess=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI GEO/SRA/BioProject/dbGaP links, full text not in PMC); Crossref record (journal-article, Science 394(6819):60-68, 199 references, no licence, one 'is-supplemented-by' relation); that supplement DOI 10.1126/science.z2scut4, which resolves to an AAAS podcast episode, not data; Zenodo (0 hits), Dryad (0 hits) searches on the identifier. Figshare's search endpoint returned 404 and is recorded as unavailable.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the abstract was available (no full text, no methods, no data availability statement). The claims about ~72 menopause symptoms and >200 hormone therapy varieties come from the abstract alone and could not be traced to any table or file.

a1_downloadable.note: There is no dataset. This is a subscription-only narrative review with no supplementary files, no accessions, and no repository deposit; the only linked 'supplement' is an AAAS podcast episode. The cohorts it reviews (Women's Health Initiative, SWAN, UK Biobank) each need registration or an access application and are not this paper's data.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No files exist, so no label column exists; any outcome would have to be assembled from third-party cohorts.

a3_inputs_present.note: No feature table of any kind is distributed with the paper.

a5_enough_rows.note: Zero rows are distributed with this review; row count is null because nothing was opened.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits, because there is nothing to download.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing to compare: no download, no API dataset record, no counts to reconcile.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable: no label exists in any distributed file.

existing_models.name: Questionnaire-based XGBoost model for early natural menopause (npj Women's Health, 2025) - XGBoost is a gradient-boosted decision tree method
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported AUC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) 0.745 on a held-out test set, with external validation AUC 0.68 on CHARLS (China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study); taken from the search result summary, not from the full paper.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved - I only saw the search snippet, not the discussion section.

existing_models.name: XGBoost model for low bone mass in menopausal women (Scientific Reports, multicentre retrospective study)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported AUC 0.918 internally and 0.910 on an external hospital dataset; from the search result summary only.

existing_models.name: Multimodal menopause-status classifier using features extracted from ultrasound reports by a large language model (Frontiers in Endocrinology, 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: 713 women from one Chinese hospital for training, 284 from a second hospital as external validation; performance numbers not retrieved. Code and analysis said to be on GitHub.

integration.partner_dataset: none - with no primary data there is nothing to join; SWAN (Study of Women's Health Across the Nation, at ICPSR) and the Women's Health Initiative (at BioLINCC) would be the candidates, but both are separate studies requiring their own registration or application.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: the review distributes no identifiers to join on.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible from this paper alone: it is a literature synthesis with no measurements, so any model would be trained entirely on other people's restricted-access cohorts.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a woman's menopause characteristics and hormone therapy details to predict her later-life disease risk.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would use per-woman records - age and type of menopause, symptom burden, genetics, and the exact hormone preparation, dose and timing - but this review supplies none; a real version would need SWAN (about 3,302 women in the public-use files) or the Women's Health Initiative, neither of which is this paper's data.
plain_idea.predict: Later-life outcomes such as cardiovascular events, fracture or dementia, measured by clinical adjudication in those cohorts, not by anything in this paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Clinicians choosing among more than 200 hormone therapy formulations have little individualised evidence, so a risk-benefit predictor would matter - but it would have to be built from cohort data obtained elsewhere, under their own access rules.

more_or_better_data.why: This review contributes zero rows of data, so by construction it is not bigger or better than the cohort data the existing menopause models used (for example 713 training women in the ultrasound study, or national survey samples).

confidence_score.why: No measurements, no replicates and no per-group counts are distributed, so nothing here supports calibrated per-prediction uncertainty.

models_beatable.why: The models found are gradient-boosted trees from 2025-2026 with modest external numbers (early-menopause AUC dropping from 0.745 internally to 0.68 on an outside cohort), which looks beatable in principle - but not with this paper, which has no data to beat them with.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails every condition: there is no baseline we could run on shared data, no feature set we would inherit, and no joinable new measurements - the review contains only text and 199 references.

ml_idea: Considered and dropped: a precision-medicine risk model mapping menopause type, timing, symptom burden and specific hormone therapy formulation to later-life cardiovascular, bone and cognitive outcomes. The review motivates the question well but provides no data; executing it would mean working from SWAN, the Women's Health Initiative or UK Biobank, each with its own registration or access application, which is a Part A1 failure under this checklist.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimates are meaningful because no data file exists to load; nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Look at the Europe PMC flags - hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, publication type 'Review' - and the Crossref relation list, which contains only a podcast. That took two minutes and killed it.

verdict_reason: Narrative review article with no data at all: subscription-only, no full text in PubMed Central, no supplementary files, no accessions, and no Zenodo or Dryad deposit. Part A1 fails outright, and the cohorts it discusses (Women's Health Initiative, SWAN, UK Biobank) are separate studies behind registration or access applications.
